title: Islamophobes are not all the same! A study of far right actors on Twitter
benchmark_measurement: Detection and classification of Islamophobic hate speech in tweets. The benchmark uses a machine learning classifier to assign tweets to one of three ordinal classes: None, Implicit, and Explicit Islamophobia, based on Bleich's definition of Islamophobia as 'indiscriminate negative attitudes or emotions directed at Islam or Muslims'.
findings: The study found that Islamophobic behavior among far-right actors on Twitter is highly heterogeneous, not monolithic. Using latent Markov modeling, the authors identified seven distinct types of users based on their quantitative, qualitative, and temporal patterns of posting Islamophobic content: None, Very Low, Low, High, Very High, Escalating, and De-escalating. A key finding is that a small number of users are responsible for the majority of Islamophobic content observed. The prevalence of Islamophobia fluctuates significantly over time, often spiking in response to real-world events like terrorist attacks. Additionally, even within this far-right cohort, implicit Islamophobia was twice as common as explicit, overt Islamophobia.
